cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here would be about sweep TIMING rather than about the defect. It must be read in-guest before it is called either way.

title: a function-static pointer was freed but left set, so the next call read and re-freed it
object: the legacy filter label, a g_strdup held in a function-static
lifetime_ender: g_free(filter_label), which does not clear the static it read from
shape: a function-static that outlives its allocation because the free does not clear it
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is the NEXT PRS_GUI_FILTER_EXPR line, which passes the stale label onward.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8:epan/prefs.c carries `filter_label = NULL;` after the free (`grep -c` = 2, the declaration plus the added clear). The form without the clear is at d3e3c00fbbe2^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.
nested_why: the object came straight from g_malloc / g_new / g_new0 / g_strdup / getline -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no wmem allocator between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../wmem-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the dangling pointer is a FUNCTION-STATIC, so the lifetime spans CALLS rather than statements -- the free and the use are in different invocations of one function, and the trigger is simply a preferences file with two of the same legacy entry. Nothing in a single call looks wrong.
